name: Protein Simulation Force Field Datasets
description: This review article provides an overview of structurally oriented experimental datasets that can be used to benchmark protein force fields, focusing on data generated by nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy and room temperature (RT) protein crystallography. We discuss what the observables are, what they tell us about structure and dynamics, what makes them useful for assessing force field accuracy, and how they can be connected to molecular dynamics simulations carried out using the force field one wishes to benchmark. We also touch on statistical issues that arise when comparing simulations with experiment. We hope this article will be particularly useful to computational researchers and trainees who develop, benchmark, or use protein force fields for molecular simulations.
evaluation_method: comparative analysis against experimental observables and simulation agreement metrics
reputation: A scholarly review of benchmark datasets for protein force fields, useful in the molecular simulation community but not a single standardized leaderboard benchmark.
notes: This is a review of datasets rather than a single benchmark; evaluation depends on the specific observable and force field, so there is no unified score or SOTA number.
